intro: I build cloud platforms, data pipelines and the infrastructure underneath AI/ML workloads. I believe the best engineering is quiet — systems that just work and let people focus on what actually matters.

Four years at Quantiphi shipping AWS platforms for Fortune 100 teams taught me that the most impactful code is often the code nobody notices. These days I'm in grad school, building things like a Kubernetes controller that keeps warm LLM caches alive during scale-down.

projects.name: cache-aware-scale-in
projects.title: Cache-aware scale-in for vLLM on Kubernetes
projects.description: A Kubernetes controller that scores each vLLM replica's KV-cache hit rate and writes it to the pod-deletion-cost annotation, so a scale-down removes the coldest replica instead of an arbitrary one — fewer warm caches thrown away, lower time to first token.
highlights: Built as a six-stage ladder: laptop prototype with fake pods → kind/k3s mock cluster → Llama 3 8B on 3 A100 replicas with llm-d routing.
Ships as an in-cluster image with RBAC, Prometheus/Loki/Grafana dashboards, and CI that runs the scale-in trial on kind for every push.

projects.name: idempotent-order-cloud-api
projects.title: Idempotent Order API
projects.description: A retry-safe order service: the Idempotency-Key is claimed in the same Postgres transaction as the order, so concurrent duplicates get the same order back instead of a second order or a 500.
highlights: Found and fixed a select-then-insert race that returned 500s under parallel retries; replaced with a single INSERT … ON CONFLICT claim.
11.7× throughput and 8.6× lower p95 at saturation after adding a threadpool and connection pool (3,558 req/s, p95 22 ms, k6 on one machine).
Deployed ALB → ECS Fargate → RDS with Terraform and GitHub Actions; Redis rate limiter; 41 tests.

projects.name: iac-drift-saas
projects.title: IaC Drift Reconciliation SaaS
projects.description: Multi-tenant pipeline that reads CloudTrail across AWS accounts, finds console changes that drifted from CloudFormation, has an LLM on Bedrock rewrite the template, validates it with cfn-lint and opens a GitHub pull request.
highlights: Five Lambdas fanned out per stack, with DynamoDB de-duplication, an SQS dead-letter queue and CloudWatch health checks every five minutes.
Self-service customer portal (FastAPI + React) on App Runner; SaaS and customer-side infrastructure in Terraform.

projects.name: parallelized-nbody-simulation-cuda-cpp
projects.title: Parallel N-body simulation
projects.description: A galaxy simulation with five solvers compared like-for-like: SIMD serial, OpenMP, a Barnes–Hut octree, and naive versus shared-memory-tiled CUDA kernels.
highlights: Removed a cross-block data race by splitting force and position updates across kernel launches.
Switched to a kick-drift-kick leapfrog integrator and measured the Barnes–Hut crossover at N ≈ 12.7K bodies under OpenMP.
